subject: Climate & Environment
title: Coral Reefs as Ecosystems
description: A fast breakdown of Coral Reefs as Ecosystems for builders.

hook.text: Coral reefs are called the rainforests of the sea. They earn that name.

buildup.text: Covering less than 1% of the ocean, they host 25% of all marine species.

discovery.text: A healthy reef supports fish, sponges, crabs, eels, sharks, and thousands of invertebrates.

twist.text: Reefs also protect coastlines — breaking wave energy by up to 97% before it hits shore.

climax.text: Half the world's reefs are already dead or severely degraded from warming and pollution.

punchline.text: Lose the reef and you lose the coast and the creatures it shelters.

quiz.question: How much wave energy can healthy coral reefs absorb?

details.summary: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor yet support roughly 25 percent of all marine species. They provide food, coastal protection, tourism revenue, and pharmaceutical resources worth hundreds of billions of dollars annually.
details.whyItMatters: Reefs are collapsing under warming oceans, acidification, and pollution. Losing them would devastate marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of half a billion people.
takeaways: Reefs support 25 percent of marine species on less than 1 percent of ocean floor
Half a billion people depend on reefs for food and income
Repeated bleaching events have killed over half of Great Barrier Reef coral

faq.question: How do coral reefs protect coastlines?
faq.answer: Reef structures break incoming wave energy by up to 97 percent, reducing coastal erosion, flooding, and storm damage. Without reefs, many tropical coastlines and small island nations would face far greater losses from storms and sea-level rise.

faq.question: Can coral reefs recover from bleaching?
faq.answer: Mild bleaching events allow recovery if temperatures return to normal within weeks. However, severe or repeated bleaching kills corals outright. Recovery takes a decade or more, and many reefs now bleach too frequently to recover between events.
